Second, several structural, material, dimensional and variant details in the description, figure briefs and claims are not traceable to input/disclosure.md or input/conversation.md (the disclosure and the conversation are word-for-word identical, so there is no second source): notably the perforations being "through its bottom", the elongate/asymmetric keying of rib and channel in claim 5, the interchangeable-cassette variant of claim 15 and the multi-depth tray, the foam-core/moulded-polymer materials, the wick's strip geometry, and the ledge/foot specifics in claim 4. Third, the added "bottom" perforation limitation creates a self-contradiction in the recited flow path, which is stated in both directions within a single paragraph and again in claims 1 and 16. No [REF:...] citations appear in the draft and prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references, so there is nothing to check under citation fidelity; as the drafting brief notes, no prior-art search was run and the available art is empty rather than merely incomplete.

findings.title: No drawing sheets exist for FIG. 1 through FIG. 5; every specification numeral is unillustrated
findings.detail: The specification describes five figures and uses thirty reference numerals, but figures/ contains only the five Markdown briefs (fig-01.md through fig-05.md) — there is no rendered-*.png for any figure, and review/figure-audit-evidence.json does not exist. A directory listing and a recursive search for *.png / rendered* return nothing. This is the single cause of both mechanical failures reported (five described figures with no sheet, thirty numerals absent from every drawing). It cannot be verified whether the visible geometry and printed numerals agree with the briefs, because no pixels exist to open. Note that the briefs themselves do distribute all thirty numerals across the five sheets (10,16,20,40,60,64,80 / 12,14,20,26,28,30,40,60 / 18,42,44,46,48,52,54,62 / 22,24,48,50,56,70,72,74 / 10,44,80,82,84,86 = 30 distinct), so the drawing plan is complete and only the rendering step is missing.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 1 is an exploded perspective view of a reusable passive cold-chain carrier, showing the insulated outer shell, the removable product tray, the removable thermal module, and the insulated lid." — figures/fig-01.md ends "## Reference numerals appearing on this sheet\n10, 16, 20, 40, 60, 64, 80", but `ls figures/` returns only fig-01.md, fig-02.md, fig-03.md, fig-04.md, fig-05.md.
findings.fix: Render one sheet per existing brief (figures/rendered-fig-01.png … rendered-fig-05.png) from the five briefs as written, which already carry every numeral, and regenerate review/figure-audit-evidence.json against the resulting image hashes. No text, numeral definition, or part need be removed or added to satisfy the check.

findings.title: Perforations located "through its bottom" and "distributed across the bottom" are not in the disclosure
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶7 and ¶61; draft/09-claims.md claim 1 and claim 7; figures/fig-01.md, figures/fig-02.md
findings.detail: The inventor says only that air "passes through perforations in the product tray" and never says where those perforations are. The candidate adds a specific location and distribution, carries it into claim 1 as a positive structural limitation of the tray and into claim 7 as a further limitation, and builds figure geometry on it. Location of an opening is a structure, and the candidate's own detailed description cannot supply support it introduced itself. The added location is also what produces the flow-path contradiction reported separately.
findings.evidence: disclosure.md: "enters the side supply passages, passes through perforations in the product tray, and returns through the lower return passage" — candidate ¶7: "The removable product tray 20 has perforations 26 through its bottom, distributed across the bottom, so that the interior of the removable product tray 20 communicates with the lower return passage 28."; claim 1: "the removable product tray having a bottom with perforations through the bottom"; claim 7: "the perforations are distributed across the bottom of the removable product tray"; figures/fig-02.md: "Perforation 26: small gaps through the thickness of the bottom panel of the tray 20, distributed across that panel".
findings.fix: Recite the perforations only as the inventor did. In ¶7 replace with "The removable product tray 20 has perforations 26 through the removable product tray 20." and delete "so that the interior of the removable product tray 20 communicates with the lower return passage 28."; in claim 1 replace "a bottom with perforations through the bottom" with "perforations through the removable product tray"; delete "and the perforations are distributed across the bottom of the removable product tray" from claim 7; in ¶61 delete the first sentence about the number and distribution of perforations; in fig-02.md change to "Perforation 26: small gaps through the wall of the tray 20 opening into the adjacent side supply passage 30" and in fig-01.md replace "a field of small round through holes distributed across the panel" with a corresponding wall depiction.

findings.title: The circulation path is recited in two mutually exclusive directions in the same paragraph
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶23 (also ¶7, ¶61); draft/09-claims.md claim 1 wherein-clause and claim 16 final step
findings.detail: With the perforations placed only through the tray bottom, air arriving in a side supply passage cannot reach those perforations before reaching the lower return passage: the return passage lies between them. The first sentence of ¶23 orders the path "side supply passages → perforations → lower return passage", while the very next sentence orders it "lower return passage → up through the bottom → payload" by stating that cooled air is delivered from below. ¶7 states the bottom perforations connect the tray interior to the return passage, which is the second order, and ¶61 states delivery runs "from the side supply passages 30 into the interior" through those same bottom holes, which is the first. Claims 1 and 16 both freeze the first order into the claim language. As written, no single geometry satisfies every statement.
findings.evidence: ¶23: "enters the side supply passages 30, passes through the perforations 26 in the removable product tray 20, and returns through the lower return passage 28 to the product region. The path is closed on itself and surrounds the removable product tray 20 on the sides and underneath, so that cooled air is delivered to the payload from below and around it"; claim 16: "through the peripheral outlet openings into the side supply passages, through perforations in the removable product tray, and back to the product region through the lower return passage".
findings.fix: Apply the same correction as for the bottom-perforation limitation: with the perforations no longer confined to the tray bottom, the disclosed order (side supply passages → perforations → lower return passage) is self-consistent throughout. In ¶23 delete "so that cooled air is delivered to the payload from below and around it and warmed air is drawn off from above it", or restate it neutrally as "so that cooled air reaches the payload around and beneath the removable product tray 20". Leave the claim 1 and claim 16 sequences as they stand, since they already track the disclosure's wording.

findings.title: Claim 5 and ¶31 add an undisclosed keying geometry for the indexing rib and mating channel
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that the rib enters a mating channel and shifts the module into the registered position. It says nothing about the rib and channel being elongate, about asymmetric placement on the frame, about a resulting single permitted orientation, about the rib meeting the channel over a range of initial positions, or about the rib drawing the module inward during descent. These are added shape, placement and function assertions, and one of them is claimed.
findings.evidence: disclosure.md: "As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages." — ¶31: "The depending indexing rib 62 and the mating channel 52 are shaped so that the rib meets the channel over a range of initial positions of the removable thermal module 40 and draws it inward as the insulated lid 60 descends... In some embodiments the depending indexing rib 62 and the mating channel 52 are elongate and asymmetrically placed on the rigid spacer frame 42, so that the removable thermal module 40 can be seated in only one orientation and the peripheral outlet openings 50 cannot be presented to the wrong side of the interior."; claim 5: "wherein the depending indexing rib and the mating channel are elongate and asymmetrically placed on the rigid spacer frame, so that the removable thermal module is seated in only one orientation."
findings.fix: Delete ¶31 in its entirety and cancel claim 5, renumbering claims 6–21 and their dependencies accordingly. The disclosed registration function is already stated in ¶29 in the inventor's own terms and claimed in claim 1.

findings.title: Claim 15 and the Variations paragraph add undisclosed variants (interchangeable cassette chemistries, multiple tray depths)
findings.detail: Neither the disclosure nor the conversation mentions cassettes of a different phase-change material, a different transport range, interchangeability without change to the frame, rib or channel, or a tray offered in more than one depth. These are added variants presented as part of the invention, and one of them is a claim limitation.
findings.evidence: ¶61: "The removable product tray 20 may be provided in more than one depth for the same insulated outer shell 10... The phase-change cassettes 44 may be exchanged for cassettes of a different phase-change material to suit a different transport range, without any change to the rigid spacer frame 42, the depending indexing rib 62, or the mating channel 52"; claim 15: "wherein the phase-change cassettes are exchangeable for cassettes of a different phase-change material without change to the rigid spacer frame, the depending indexing rib, or the mating channel." The disclosure says only "conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame" and "a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes".
findings.fix: Delete the second and third sentences of ¶61 and cancel claim 15, renumbering the remaining claims. Retain the last paragraph of ¶63, which restates the inventor's own statement that the wick and the indicator are supported optional features.

findings.title: Undisclosed materials of construction asserted for the shell, lid and spacer frame
findings.detail: The disclosure identifies the shell and lid only as "insulated" and the frame only as "rigid", and says the carrier is reusable. It names no material. "Rigid foam core within a washable outer skin" and "moulded polymer" are specific material constructions introduced by the candidate; common engineering knowledge and plausibility are not source support.
findings.evidence: ¶5: "The insulated outer shell 10, the insulated lid 60, and the walls that bound the interior are of insulating construction, for example a rigid foam core within a washable outer skin, so that the carrier can be cleaned, stacked, and returned for reuse."; ¶13: "The rigid spacer frame 42 is a self-supporting frame body, for example of moulded polymer, stiff enough that the phase-change cassettes 44 it carries do not close the passages formed in it." Disclosure: "A reusable passive cold-chain carrier has an insulated outer shell... and an insulated lid"; "The thermal module is a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes."
findings.fix: In ¶5 delete ", for example a rigid foam core within a washable outer skin," leaving "are of insulating construction". In ¶13 delete ", for example of moulded polymer," leaving "The rigid spacer frame 42 is a self-supporting rigid frame body".

findings.title: Undisclosed wick and pull-tab geometry (strip sized to the channel, tab as an end extension standing above the rim)
findings.detail: The inventor discloses that a removable absorbent wick lies in the shallow condensate channel and that a pull tab on the wick remains accessible when the tray is removed. Nothing states that the wick is a strip, that it is sized to the length of the channel, that the tab is an extension of that strip at one end, or that the tab stands above the channel rim. The figure brief then makes that same geometry the depicted structure, so the drawing would be the only source for it.
findings.evidence: disclosure.md: "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray... A pull tab on the wick remains accessible when the product tray is removed" — ¶43: "In some embodiments the removable absorbent wick 72 is a strip of absorbent material sized to the length of the shallow condensate channel 70, and the pull tab 74 is an extension of that strip at one end that stands above the rim of the shallow condensate channel 70."; figures/fig-04.md: "Pull tab 74: a short narrow tongue continuous with the inboard end of the wick 72, rising out of the channel 70 above the rim of the trough and clear of the wall 24."
findings.fix: Delete the last sentence of ¶43. In fig-04.md, reduce the two entries to the disclosed relationship: "Removable absorbent wick 72: an elongate body lying in the trough of the channel 70" and "Pull tab 74: a tab on the wick 72, drawn so that it is reachable from above when the tray is removed", deleting "occupying most of the width of the trough and standing lower than its rim" and "rising out of the channel 70 above the rim of the trough and clear of the wall 24".

findings.title: Claim 4 recites ledge and resilient-foot specifics that the disclosure does not give
findings.detail: The disclosure says the closing movement "presses resilient feet of the spacer frame against ledges of the shell so that the module cannot lift away from the tray during transport" and nothing more. That the ledges project inward from the shell side walls, that they sit at the level at which the module is seated, that the feet are compliant limbs of the frame, that they remain loaded while the carrier is closed and relax when the lid is opened, and that the module then lifts out by hand without a tool, are all candidate additions, and the first four are claimed.
findings.evidence: ¶35: "The ledges 18 project inward from the shell side walls 14 at the level at which the removable thermal module 40 is seated. The resilient feet 54 are compliant limbs of the rigid spacer frame 42, and the closing insulated lid 60 deflects them against the ledges 18 so that they remain loaded while the carrier is closed... When the insulated lid 60 is opened, the resilient feet 54 relax and the removable thermal module 40 lifts out by hand without a tool."; claim 4: "wherein the ledges project inward from the shell side walls at a level at which the removable thermal module is seated, and the resilient feet are compliant limbs of the rigid spacer frame that remain loaded against the ledges while the carrier is closed and relax when the insulated lid is opened."
findings.fix: Cancel claim 4 and renumber. In ¶35 keep the first sentence (which tracks the disclosure verbatim) and the sentence about the load holding the module down, and delete "The ledges 18 project inward from the shell side walls 14 at the level at which the removable thermal module 40 is seated. The resilient feet 54 are compliant limbs of the rigid spacer frame 42, and the closing insulated lid 60 deflects them against the ledges 18 so that they remain loaded while the carrier is closed." and the final sentence about relaxing and lifting out without a tool. In fig-03.md, replace "a downwardly projecting hatched limb of reduced thickness at each outboard lower corner of the frame 42" with "a downwardly projecting foot at each outboard lower corner of the frame 42".

findings.title: Tray feet "spaced apart" and a return passage "continuous from one side to the other" are added relationships
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that the tray is "suspended above the shell floor by feet so that a lower return passage remains under the tray". The candidate adds a spacing relationship between the feet and a continuity requirement for the return passage across the full width of the shell, claims it, and builds the FIG. 2 geometry on it. The continuity assertion is a functional flow relationship, not merely the inherent gap implied by plural feet.
findings.evidence: ¶7: "The tray feet 22 are spaced apart from one another so that the lower return passage 28 is continuous beneath the removable product tray 20 from one side of the insulated outer shell 10 to the other."; claim 7: "wherein the tray feet are spaced apart from one another so that the lower return passage is continuous beneath the removable product tray from one side of the insulated outer shell to the other"; figures/fig-02.md: "Short hatched supports stand between the bottom panel and the shell floor 12, spaced apart along the width so that the space between them runs continuously from left to right."
findings.fix: Delete that sentence from ¶7 and cancel claim 7 (whose remaining half is addressed by the perforation fix), renumbering. In fig-02.md replace the quoted sentence with "Short hatched supports stand between the bottom panel and the shell floor 12." and, in the Lower return passage 28 entry, delete "continuous from left to right between the short supports".

findings.title: Claim 14 recites a structural separation of the indicator interior from the circulation path that the disclosure does not state
findings.detail: The inventor's statement is functional and one sentence long: "The indicator does not control airflow." The candidate converts that into a structural limitation — that the indicator has an interior and that this interior is separate from the circulation path — and also asserts it in the description and in the FIG. 5 brief. The invariance of the circulation path between the retained and exposed states follows from the disclosed sentence; the structural separation of interiors does not.
findings.evidence: disclosure.md: "The indicator does not control airflow." — claim 14: "wherein the mechanical exposure indicator does not control airflow, an interior of the mechanical exposure indicator being separate from the circulation path and the circulation path being the same whether the indicator stem is retained by the temperature-responsive latch or has moved to the latched exposed position."; ¶51: "The interior of the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is separate from the circulation path"; figures/fig-05.md: "The interior of the indicator 80 is separate from the interior of the carrier and does not open into any internal passage of the carrier."
findings.fix: In claim 14 delete "an interior of the mechanical exposure indicator being separate from the circulation path and", leaving the functional recitation plus the path-invariance clause. Delete the sentence "The interior of the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is separate from the circulation path" from ¶51 and the corresponding Relationships bullet from fig-05.md.

findings.title: Assertion that no face of the payload contacts a cassette
findings.detail: The disclosure places the spacer frame above the tray and below the lid and says the cassettes are opposed, but never states that the payload is out of contact with a cassette, nor that the payload is conditioned by air rather than by conduction. The background separately identifies direct contact as a problem of prior containers, which makes this sentence read as an advantage assertion rather than a disclosed fact. I am less certain here than on the other fidelity items, because non-contact is close to a consequence of the frame resting above the tray; it is flagged as minor for that reason.
findings.evidence: ¶17: "and no face of the payload is in contact with a phase-change cassette 44. The payload is conditioned by the air that has passed the phase-change cassettes 44, rather than by conduction into a cassette lying on top of it." Disclosure: "The spacer frame rests above the product tray and below the lid."
findings.fix: Delete "and no face of the payload is in contact with a phase-change cassette 44" and the following sentence, leaving the disclosed observation that air entering between the opposed cassettes is exposed to two cooled faces at once.

findings.title: FIG. 5 geometry places a cassette against the shell wall, which conflicts with the module geometry of FIG. 3
findings.detail: FIG. 3 and the description put each cassette inside the spacer frame with a downward guide duct and an outboard frame web between the cassette's outboard surface and the shell side wall. FIG. 5 instead shows a cassette standing close to the shell's inner surface with the stem touching both, leaving no room for the duct or the outboard web. The description itself is neutral — it says only that the stem is "thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette 44" — so the conflict is between the two figure briefs, and it will be baked into the rendered sheets. Reported as minor because FIG. 5 is expressly a schematic wall-region section.
findings.evidence: figures/fig-05.md: "Phase-change cassette 44: a slab-like body inside the carrier at the right of the view... standing close to the inner surface of the shell 10 with the inner end of the stem 82 between them and touching both." versus figures/fig-03.md: "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42", and ¶15: "Each downward guide duct 48 extends downward beside one of the phase-change cassettes 44".
findings.fix: In fig-05.md, change the cassette entry to "Phase-change cassette 44: a slab-like body inside the carrier at the right of the view, spaced from the inner surface of the shell 10, with the inner end of the stem 82 lying at that inner surface facing the cassette 44", and change the first Relationships bullet to "The stem 82 extends from the inner surface of the shell 10, through the thickness of the shell 10, into the interior of the indicator 80, and is thermally coupled to the cassette 44." This matches the disclosed "thermally coupled" wording without asserting contact.

findings.title: Sectional views FIG. 2 through FIG. 5 have no cutting-plane line or section designation on any view
findings.detail: Four of the five figures are sectional views, and FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 are enlargements of regions of the carrier, yet no brief places a broken cutting-plane line with a matching designation at each end and arrows in the viewing direction on any view, and the Brief Description never states which view a section is taken on. Under 37 CFR 1.84(h)(3) the plane of a section must be indicated on the view from which it is taken. Because no sheets have been rendered, this is a defect in the briefs rather than in verified pixels.
findings.evidence: draft/07-drawings.md: "FIG. 2 is a schematic vertical sectional view of the carrier in a closed condition"; "FIG. 3 is an enlarged schematic sectional view of an upper region of the carrier"; figures/fig-01.md "## Reference numerals appearing on this sheet\n10, 16, 20, 40, 60, 64, 80" — no cutting-plane line is specified anywhere in fig-01.md, and fig-02.md likewise specifies none for FIG. 3, FIG. 4 or FIG. 5.
findings.fix: Add to fig-01.md a broken cutting-plane line across the shell 10 with the designation 2-2 at each end and both arrows pointing in the viewing direction of FIG. 2 (no numeral leaders on the designations), and amend draft/07-drawings.md to read "FIG. 2 is a schematic vertical sectional view taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 1...". For FIG. 3, FIG. 4 and FIG. 5, add to fig-02.md a broken circle or bracket around the upper region, the lateral region and the indicator wall region respectively, and amend the Brief Description to identify each as an enlarged view of the correspondingly indicated region of FIG. 2.

# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

A reusable passive cold-chain carrier has an insulated outer shell, a removable product tray, a removable thermal module, and an insulated lid. The product tray is suspended above the shell floor by feet so that a lower return passage remains under the tray. The tray side walls are spaced inward from the shell side walls to form two side supply passages.

The thermal module is a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes. The spacer frame rests above the product tray and below the lid. It includes a central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, and peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages. Warm air rising from the product region enters the central inlet, divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts, enters the side supply passages, passes through perforations in the product tray, and returns through the lower return passage. The carrier is passive. It has no fan, pump, or powered air mover.

The lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages. A compressible lid gasket seals against the upper edge of the shell after registration. The same closing movement presses resilient feet of the spacer frame against ledges of the shell so that the module cannot lift away from the tray during transport.

A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray. Openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel. A pull tab on the wick remains accessible when the product tray is removed, allowing the wick to be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette.

The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch. If that cassette softens enough to release the latch, a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position. The indication remains exposed after the cassette cools again and is reset manually only after the carrier is opened. The indicator does not control airflow.

For use, conditioned cassettes are fitted to the spacer frame, products are placed in the tray, the thermal module is placed above the tray, and the lid is closed to register and retain the module. The disclosed essential relationship is the registered passive circulation path around the removable tray and opposed cassettes, combined with lid-driven registration of the thermal module. The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features.

1	In the following description, the terms upper, lower, above, below, inward, and outward refer to the carrier in its normal upright attitude of use, in which the insulated lid is uppermost. The described embodiments illustrate the invention and do not limit it. FIG. 1 through FIG. 6 show one carrier, each view showing the parts that view is concerned with, and a part introduced in one view is referred to elsewhere in this description whether or not it is shown in every view.
2	
3	## Overview of the carrier
4	
5	Referring to FIG. 1 and FIG. 2, a reusable passive cold-chain carrier includes an insulated outer shell 10, a removable product tray 20, a removable thermal module 40, and an insulated lid 60. The insulated outer shell 10 has a shell floor 12, shell side walls 14 rising from the shell floor 12, and an upper edge 16 at the top of the shell side walls 14. The insulated outer shell 10, the insulated lid 60, and the walls that bound the interior are of insulating construction, so that the carrier can be returned for reuse.
6	
7	Referring also to FIG. 5, the removable product tray 20 receives the payload. The removable product tray 20 has tray side walls 24 and tray feet 22. The tray feet 22 stand on the shell floor 12 and suspend the removable product tray 20 above the shell floor 12, so that a lower return passage 28 remains under the removable product tray 20. The tray side walls 24 are spaced inward from the shell side walls 14 to form two side supply passages 30, each side supply passage 30 extending upward from the lower return passage 28 alongside the removable product tray 20. The removable product tray 20 has perforations 26 through the removable product tray 20.
8	
9	The removable product tray 20 lifts out of the insulated outer shell 10 as a unit, with the payload in it, once the removable thermal module 40 has been taken out. Loading and unloading therefore do not disturb the passages, because the passages are formed by the position that the removable product tray 20 takes up when it is returned to the insulated outer shell 10 and not by any separate ducting that has to be assembled.
10	
11	## The removable thermal module
12	
13	Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 3, and FIG. 4, the removable thermal module 40 includes a rigid spacer frame 42 holding two opposed phase-change cassettes 44. The rigid spacer frame 42 is a rigid frame body. The rigid spacer frame 42 rests above the removable product tray 20 and below the insulated lid 60, so that the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out as one piece and the two phase-change cassettes 44 travel with it.
14	
15	The rigid spacer frame 42 includes a central inlet opening 46 through its upper region, two downward guide ducts 48 beside the phase-change cassettes 44, and peripheral outlet openings 50. Each phase-change cassette 44 is a sealed cassette of phase-change material that is conditioned before use, and the two phase-change cassettes 44 are held on opposite sides of the central inlet opening 46 with their faces mutually opposed. Each downward guide duct 48 extends downward beside one of the phase-change cassettes 44 and opens at its lower end. The peripheral outlet openings 50 lie at the periphery of the rigid spacer frame 42 and are aligned with the side supply passages 30 when the removable thermal module 40 is in a registered position.
16	
17	Because the two phase-change cassettes 44 are opposed and are held apart by the rigid spacer frame 42, the air that enters between them is exposed to two cooled faces at once.
18	
19	## The registered passive circulation path
20	
21	The carrier is passive. It has no fan, pump, or powered air mover. Circulation is produced by the density difference between the air warmed by the payload and the air cooled at the faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, and the geometry of the carrier gives that difference a single closed path to follow.
22	
23	In use, warm air rising from a product region within the removable product tray 20 enters the central inlet opening 46, divides along faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, descends through the downward guide ducts 48, enters the side supply passages 30, passes through the perforations 26 in the removable product tray 20, and returns through the lower return passage 28 to the product region. The path is closed on itself and surrounds the removable product tray 20 on the sides and underneath, so that cooled air reaches the payload around and beneath the removable product tray 20.
24	
25	The path exists only when the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30. If the removable thermal module 40 is set down out of position, the peripheral outlet openings 50 discharge against the tray side walls 24 or against the shell side walls 14, the descending limb of the path is blocked, and the carrier behaves as a plain insulated box. This is the failure that the registration described below is directed to, and it is a failure that gives no outward sign, because a removable thermal module 40 that is merely set in place looks the same whether or not it is correctly positioned.
26	
27	## Lid-driven registration and retention
28	
29	Referring to FIG. 1, FIG. 3, and FIG. 4, the insulated lid 60 carries a depending indexing rib 62, and the rigid spacer frame 42 has a mating channel 52 that receives the depending indexing rib 62. As the insulated lid 60 closes, the depending indexing rib 62 enters the mating channel 52 and shifts the removable thermal module 40 into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30. The registration is therefore performed by the act of closing the carrier. The person who packs the carrier is not required to align the removable thermal module 40, and cannot leave it misaligned, because the insulated lid 60 does not come down onto the upper edge 16 without carrying the removable thermal module 40 into position.
30	
31	A compressible lid gasket 64 on the insulated lid 60 seals against the upper edge 16 of the insulated outer shell 10 after registration. The order of these two events matters. The depending indexing rib 62 engages the mating channel 52 and completes the registration while the compressible lid gasket 64 is still clear of the upper edge 16, so that the removable thermal module 40 is free to be shifted by the depending indexing rib 62 and is not being asked to move after the interior has been closed off. Only then does continued closing compress the compressible lid gasket 64 against the upper edge 16 and seal the interior.
32	
33	Referring to FIG. 4, the same closing movement presses resilient feet 54 of the rigid spacer frame 42 against ledges 18 of the insulated outer shell 10, so that the removable thermal module 40 cannot lift away from the removable product tray 20 during transport. That pressing holds the removable thermal module 40 down against handling, tilting, and vibration in transit, which would otherwise let the removable thermal module 40 rise and break the overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 50 and the side supply passages 30.
34	
35	Registration and retention are thus produced by the same movement that a user has to make in any event. Nothing has to be latched, clamped, or checked separately, and there is no state in which the carrier is closed and sealed but the circulation path is not established.
36	
37	## Condensate handling and the removable wick
38	
39	Referring to FIG. 5, a shallow condensate channel 70 extends around the removable product tray 20, and a removable absorbent wick 72 lies in the shallow condensate channel 70. Condensate discharge openings 56 at lower ends of the downward guide ducts 48 discharge condensate into the shallow condensate channel 70. Moisture that condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56, rather than collecting on the payload or standing in the bottom of the interior.
40	
41	The removable absorbent wick 72 has a pull tab 74. The pull tab 74 remains accessible when the removable product tray 20 is removed, so that the removable absorbent wick 72 is drawn out of the shallow condensate channel 70 and replaced without opening a phase-change cassette 44 and without dismantling the removable thermal module 40. Routine servicing between journeys therefore does not require handling of the sealed phase-change cassettes 44, which are conditioned items that should be returned to conditioning intact. Withdrawing the removable absorbent wick 72 from the shallow condensate channel 70 by the pull tab 74 and placing a replacement absorbent wick in the shallow condensate channel 70 restores the carrier for the next journey.
42	
43	## Mechanical exposure indicator
44	
45	Referring to FIG. 6, the insulated outer shell 10 includes a mechanical exposure indicator 80 visible from outside. An indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette 44 and is retained by a temperature-responsive latch 84. A spring 86 acts on the indicator stem 82 in the outward direction and is held by the temperature-responsive latch 84 while the phase-change cassette 44 remains in condition.
46	
47	If that phase-change cassette 44 softens enough to release the temperature-responsive latch 84, the spring 86 moves the indicator stem 82 to a latched exposed position. The indication remains exposed after the phase-change cassette 44 cools again, and is reset manually only after the carrier is opened. The value of this behaviour is that a payload which was warmed part way through a journey and then cooled again arrives at a temperature that looks correct, and the contents alone give the recipient no way to know what happened. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 records the event in the structure of the carrier and holds the record until a person opens the carrier and deliberately resets it.
48	
49	The mechanical exposure indicator 80 does not control airflow. The circulation path is the same whether the indicator stem 82 is retained or has moved to the latched exposed position. The thermal condition being reported is taken directly from a phase-change cassette 44, that is, from the reserve that actually conditions the payload, and no electrical power, battery, or logging device is required for the indication.
50	
51	## Method of passively conditioning a payload
52	
53	In use, conditioned phase-change cassettes 44 are fitted to the rigid spacer frame 42 to form the removable thermal module 40, products are placed in the removable product tray 20, the removable product tray 20 is placed in the insulated outer shell 10 on its tray feet 22, the removable thermal module 40 is placed above the removable product tray 20, and the insulated lid 60 is closed. Closing the insulated lid 60 brings the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 52, shifts the removable thermal module 40 into the registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 50 overlap the side supply passages 30, presses the resilient feet 54 against the ledges 18, and then compresses the compressible lid gasket 64 against the upper edge 16. Air then circulates passively along the path described above for the duration of the journey.
54	
55	At the destination the insulated lid 60 is opened, the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out, and the removable product tray 20 is lifted out with the payload in it. Between journeys the removable absorbent wick 72 is withdrawn from the shallow condensate channel 70 by the pull tab 74 and replaced, the phase-change cassettes 44 are returned for conditioning, and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is reset by hand if it has moved to the latched exposed position.
56	
57	## Variations
58	
59	The removable absorbent wick 72 and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 are optional features. A carrier may be built with the registered passive circulation path and the lid-driven registration alone, or with either optional feature separately, or with both. Features described in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another where the combination is physically consistent. The claims that follow define the invention, and each claim is to be read in the light of the whole of this description.
60

==> 04-field.md <==
The present disclosure relates to reusable insulated carriers for temperature-controlled distribution of payloads, and more particularly to a passive carrier in which a removable thermal module holding phase-change cassettes is registered by closing an insulated lid so that a circulation path is established around a removable product tray without any powered air mover.

==> 05-background.md <==
Temperature-sensitive payloads such as medicines, diagnostic samples, and perishable foods are frequently distributed in insulated containers that carry their own thermal reserve. A container of this kind is loaded at a packing point, handed to one or more carriers, and opened at a destination that may be many hours away. Because the container travels unattended and often without electrical power, the thermal behaviour of the container has to be set at the moment of closing and cannot be corrected in transit.

Two practical difficulties dominate the use of such containers. The first is the distribution of cold within the payload space. A thermal reserve placed against one wall, or laid directly on top of a payload, cools the material nearest to it strongly and the material farthest from it weakly, so the payload experiences a spread of temperatures. Direct contact between the thermal reserve and the payload can drive the contacted items below the intended range while more distant items drift above it. Moving air distributes the effect of the reserve more evenly, but a fan, pump, or other powered air mover adds a battery, a failure mode, and a service burden, and is unwelcome in a container that has to be returned and used again.

The second difficulty is that a container which relies on an internal air path only performs as intended if that path is actually present when the container is closed. Loose internal components are lifted, rotated, or nudged during loading and during transport. If the passages that are supposed to carry conditioned air downward are displaced relative to the passages that are supposed to carry it back, the intended path is broken and the container behaves as an ordinary insulated box, without any outward sign that anything is wrong. Placing that responsibility on the person who packs the container is unreliable, because a component that is merely set in place looks the same whether or not it is correctly positioned.

Related handling problems arise in reusable service. Condensate forms on cold surfaces inside a closed container and collects where it is difficult to reach. Removing it commonly means handling the thermal reserve itself, which is undesirable when the reserve is a sealed phase-change cassette that should not be opened in the field. Finally, a payload that has been briefly warmed can arrive at a temperature that appears correct, so a recipient inspecting the container at delivery cannot tell from the contents alone whether the thermal reserve lost its condition earlier in the journey.

There remains a need for a reusable passive carrier in which the internal circulation path is established positively by the act of closing the container, in which the thermal reserve is held in that established relationship during transport, and in which routine servicing and evidence of thermal exposure are available without opening the thermal reserve.

==> 06-summary.md <==
A reusable passive cold-chain carrier is disclosed. The carrier includes an insulated outer shell, a removable product tray, a removable thermal module, and an insulated lid.

The removable product tray is suspended above a shell floor by tray feet so that a lower return passage remains under the removable product tray. Tray side walls of the removable product tray are spaced inward from shell side walls of the insulated outer shell to form two side supply passages. The removable product tray has perforations.

The removable thermal module includes a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes. The rigid spacer frame rests above the removable product tray and below the insulated lid. The rigid spacer frame includes a central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the phase-change cassettes, and peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages.

The carrier is passive and has no fan, pump, or powered air mover. Warm air rising from a product region enters the central inlet opening, divides along faces of the phase-change cassettes, descends through the downward guide ducts, enters the side supply passages, passes through the perforations in the removable product tray, and returns through the lower return passage. The circulation path therefore surrounds the payload rather than acting on it from one side, and it is driven by the density difference that the phase-change cassettes themselves create.

The insulated lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the insulated lid closes, the depending indexing rib enters a mating channel in the rigid spacer frame and shifts the removable thermal module into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings overlap the side supply passages. The act of closing the carrier therefore establishes the circulation path, instead of relying on the person who packs the carrier to place the removable thermal module accurately. A compressible lid gasket seals against an upper edge of the insulated outer shell after registration, so the removable thermal module is aligned before the interior is closed off. The same closing movement presses resilient feet of the rigid spacer frame against ledges of the insulated outer shell so that the removable thermal module cannot lift away from the removable product tray during transport.

In some embodiments, a removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the removable product tray, and condensate discharge openings at lower ends of the downward guide ducts discharge condensate into the shallow condensate channel. A pull tab on the removable absorbent wick remains accessible when the removable product tray is removed, allowing the removable absorbent wick to be replaced without opening a phase-change cassette.

In some embodiments, the insulated outer shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch. If that phase-change cassette softens enough to release the temperature-responsive latch, a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position. The indication remains exposed after the phase-change cassette cools again and is reset manually only after the carrier is opened. The mechanical exposure indicator does not control airflow.

Methods are also disclosed, including a method of passively conditioning a payload in which conditioned phase-change cassettes are fitted to the rigid spacer frame, products are placed in the removable product tray, the removable thermal module is placed above the removable product tray, and the insulated lid is closed to register and retain the removable thermal module, and a method of servicing the carrier between uses.

Tray feet leave a return passage beneath the tray, whose side walls are spaced inward from the shell side walls to form two side supply passages. content.text: I've read the sources, every draft section, all six figure briefs, and the prior-art index. Here are my findings.

input.summary:
Workspace conditions first, because they bound the review: figures/ contains only six Markdown briefs — there is no rendered-*.png for any figure — and review/figure-audit-evidence.json does not exist, so no pixel, OCR, leader, hatch-angle or cutting-plane-endpoint evidence could be checked. Every figure finding below is against the briefs read as the drawing specification. (The absent sheets and the 30 numerals absent from any drawing are already the two mechanical failures and are not re-reported as findings.) prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and the draft contains no [REF:...] citation, so there is no citation issue; per the drafting brief, the art supplied to this draft may be incomplete.

On substance the draft tracks the inventor's disclosure closely. Every independent and dependent claim limitation traces to a disclosed sentence (shell/tray/module/lid, tray feet and lower return passage, inward-spaced tray walls and two side supply passages, rigid spacer frame with central inlet, two downward guide ducts and peripheral outlet openings, the closed passive path, lid rib into mating channel with registration, gasket, resilient feet on ledges, wick/pull tab/condensate channel, and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator). I found no claim broader than the description, no element recited that the description omits, and consistent one-name-per-part usage across summary, description, claims, numerals.md and the briefs.

The defects are three geometric inconsistencies in the drawing briefs against the description and against each other — the central inlet opening is briefed opening toward the lid rather than toward the product region the text says air rises from; FIG. 5 places the condensate discharge opening at the shell floor in a region FIG. 2 does not contain it; FIG. 6 draws a phase-change cassette lying against the shell side wall in direct contact with the indicator stem, contradicting FIG. 3/FIG. 4 and adding a coupling relationship the disclosure states only as "thermally coupled" — plus four smaller wording and brief items. Each has a fix available in the existing text or briefs from disclosed matter.

findings.title: Central inlet opening 46 is briefed and described as facing the lid, but the recited circulation has air rising from the product region below enter it
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md ("Central inlet opening 46" bullet); draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The removable thermal module" (¶ beginning "The rigid spacer frame 42 includes") and "The registered passive circulation path"; figures/FIG-2.md
findings.detail: The disclosure says only "It includes a central inlet opening" and "Warm air rising from the product region enters the central inlet, divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts" — it does not place the opening. The candidate placed it "through its upper region" and FIG-3 briefs it as a gap in the upper web that is "open upward toward the lid 60", with the same brief stating that "The rib 62 is engaged in the channel 52 while the lid 60 lies across the upper web of the frame 42". In that geometry the only side of opening 46 facing away from the frame interior is closed off by the lid, so air rising from the product region cannot enter it, and the entrance from the tray is instead the frame's open underside. FIG-2 reads the same opening the opposite way, as facing the payload: "The interior of the tray 20 is open upward toward the central opening of the module 40." One of the two briefs must be wrong, and the description's placement of the inlet in the frame's "upper region" is itself an addition to the source. FIG-3 also routes the inter-cassette space to the ducts "around their lower parts", which lets air that entered from below leave at the bottom without descending along the cassette faces as the text recites.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-3.md: "Central inlet opening 46: one rectangular gap through the upper web of the frame 42, at the centre of the width, open upward toward the lid 60 and downward into the frame interior." / "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 above it and with both ducts 48 around their lower parts." — draft/08-detailed-description.md: "The rigid spacer frame 42 includes a central inlet opening 46 through its upper region" and "warm air rising from a product region within the removable product tray 20 enters the central inlet opening 46, divides along faces of the phase-change cassettes 44, descends through the downward guide ducts 48" — figures/FIG-2.md: "The interior of the tray 20 is open upward toward the central opening of the module 40."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md write "a central inlet opening 46 at the centre of the rigid spacer frame 42 and facing the product region within the removable product tray 20". In figures/FIG-3.md change the bullet to: "Central inlet opening 46: one rectangular gap at the centre of the width of the frame 42, opening downward toward the interior of the tray 20 and upward into the blank open space between the two cassettes 44, the lower web portions of the frame 42 closing the underside of the frame 42 on each side of it." and change the relationship line to: "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and with both ducts 48 across the upper parts of the cassettes 44, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and turns into the ducts 48."

findings.title: FIG. 5 places condensate discharge opening 56 at the shell floor, in a region FIG. 2 does not contain it and where the guide ducts are not
findings.where: figures/FIG-5.md ("Condensate discharge opening 56" bullet and relationship list); figures/FIG-2.md (broken-circle paragraph); figures/FIG-4.md; draft/07-drawings.md, FIG. 5 sentence
findings.detail: FIG. 5 is expressly the enlargement of FIG. 2's right-hand lower circle, which FIG-2 briefs as enclosing only the floor trough and the lower right of the tray. FIG-5 nevertheless puts a hatched web spanning the upper part of that view, with a descending passage through it ending in opening 56 just above the channel — structure the parent view does not have at that location. It also contradicts the description and FIG. 4: opening 56 is defined as being at the lower end of downward guide duct 48, and duct 48 belongs to the module above the tray, where FIG-4 shows it "running downward and open at its lower end". The web is left "unnumbered" precisely because no numbered part can sit there. Naming it 42/48 would move the module to the shell floor; the correct correction is to show 56 where the duct lower end actually is.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-5.md: "Condensate discharge opening 56: a downwardly opening gap in an unnumbered hatched web that spans the upper part of the view, at the lower end of a descending passage through that web, positioned above the channel 70." — figures/FIG-2.md: "one around the right trough of the shell floor 12 and the lower right of the tray 20" — draft/08-detailed-description.md: "Condensate discharge openings 56 at lower ends of the downward guide ducts 48 discharge condensate into the shallow condensate channel 70."
findings.fix: Delete the "Condensate discharge opening 56" bullet and the line "The condensate discharge opening 56 opens downward toward the trough of the channel 70." from figures/FIG-5.md and remove 56 from its numeral list. Add to figures/FIG-4.md: "Condensate discharge opening 56: a downwardly opening gap at the lower end of the duct 48 in the underside of the frame 42, opening downward above the upper end of the side supply passage 30." and add 56 to that sheet's numeral list. In draft/07-drawings.md end the FIG. 4 sentence "... bearing on a ledge of the insulated outer shell, and a condensate discharge opening at a lower end of a downward guide duct", and end the FIG. 5 sentence "... showing the shallow condensate channel and the removable absorbent wick." In draft/08-detailed-description.md open that paragraph "Referring to FIG. 4 and FIG. 5, ...".

findings.title: FIG. 6 draws a phase-change cassette lying against the shell side wall and touching the indicator stem, contradicting FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 and going beyond "thermally coupled"
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md ("Phase-change cassette 44" bullet and relationship list); against draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The removable thermal module" and "Mechanical exposure indicator"; figures/FIG-3.md, figures/FIG-4.md
findings.detail: Both sources say only that the stem is "thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette"; neither states contact, nor that a cassette lies against the shell wall. Everywhere else in the application the cassettes are held inside the rigid spacer frame with the guide duct and the frame's outboard web between a cassette and the shell side wall, so nothing at the inner surface of the shell side wall can be a cassette. One is critical: FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, stating it is "open toward the bore and open at its outer side" and fixing the axial depth of the stem's outer end "within the housing and short of that outer side" - depth and port relationships the disclosure never states and which the v10 functional-surface rule treats as substantive even in a schematic view. Two are verified internal inconsistencies: FIG-3 asserts the inter-cassette space "communicates with both ducts 48" while describing an upper web continuous across the full width with the ducts outboard of the cassettes, so the described elements leave no path for the disclosed sequence; and FIG-1 shows the lid turned over with its underside toward the viewer while simultaneously stating the gasket is "positioned to face the upper edge 16", the module recess is "directly below the depending indexing rib 62", and the lid "lies above the module 40 on the same upright axis". Two are minor: the Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism ("condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48"), and claim 16 says tray removal is "thereby exposing a pull tab" where the disclosure and description say the tab "remains accessible". Each finding carries a filing-clean fix; no rendered image was inspected.

## Mechanical checks that did not pass

- **Source fidelity is clean before rendering** (fail): Full source-fidelity preflight run. I built a complete ledger over all 17 claims (three independent: apparatus claim 1, method claim 12, servicing method claim 16), every one of the 30 entries in draft/numerals.md, every numbered and unnumbered part called out in the six figure briefs, the Brief Description of Drawings, and every specific structure, relationship, result, operating condition, and variant in the Summary and Detailed Description, tracing each to an exact affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md (the conversation's single USER passage is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing). The bulk of the text traces cleanly and verbatim: the four bodies; tray feet and the lower return passage; tray side walls spaced inward forming two side supply passages; perforations; the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes and resting above the tray and below the lid; the central inlet opening, two downward guide ducts beside the cassettes, and peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages; the full passive flow sequence and the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative limitation; the depending indexing rib entering the mating channel and shifting the module to the registered overlap position; the gasket sealing against the upper edge after registration; resilient feet pressed against shell ledges so the module cannot lift; the wick, shallow condensate channel, lower-end condensate discharge openings, and pull tab accessible when the tray is removed; and the whole exposure-indicator chain (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, irreversibility, manual reset after opening, no airflow control). Both optional features are recited as optional, matching "The wick and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator are supported optional features." Numeral hygiene checked: all 30 numerals appear in the description and on at least one figure, each denot
  - FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, with an outer-side opening and a stated stem depth within it
  - FIG-3 asserts the space between the cassettes communicates with both guide ducts, but the geometry it describes leaves no path
  - FIG-1 shows the lid turned over yet states relationships that hold only for an upright, axially aligned lid
  - Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism inside the guide ducts
  - Claim 16 says tray removal exposes the pull tab, where the disclosure and description say the tab remains accessible

## Reviewer findings

- **[critical] FIG-6 verbalizes an undisclosed indicator housing as a functional port, with an outer-side opening and a stated stem depth within it** (figures/FIG-6.md, bullet "Mechanical exposure indicator 80"; and figures/FIG-2.md, bullet "Shell side wall 14" ("A small) - The brief does not merely give the disclosed indicator a generic outline; it assigns the enclosure a technical function and states relationships the inventor never disclosed: that the enclosure is open toward the bore, that it is open at its outer side, that its interior is aligned with the bore, and that the outer end of the stem lies within the enclosure and short of that outer side in the retained condition. Which end of a port is open and how deep a member sits relative to that opening is functional-surface geometry and is substantive even in a view the brief calls schematic. No affirmative USER passage discloses any housing, any outer-side opening, or the axial position of the stem's outer end relative to such an opening. The disclosure discloses only that the indicator is visible from outside, that the stem is thermally coupled to one cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch, and that a spring moves the stem to a latched exposed position; it says nothing about the enclosure that renders it visible or where the stem sits before actuation. The claims and description are correspondingly silent, so this geometry originates only in the figure brief.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-6.md replace the "Mechanical exposure indicator 80" bullet with: "Mechanical exposure indicator 80: the indicator assembly at the outer surface of the shell side wall 14, comprising the stem 82, the latch 84 and the spring 86, the assembly shown schematically within an unnumbered plain outline and the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the indicator 80 is shown in the retained condition, the stem 82 not yet having been moved by the spring 86 to the latched exposed position in which it is visible from outside the carrier." Delete the clauses "open toward the bore and open at its outer side, its interior blank and aligned with the bore, the outer end of the stem 82 lying within the housing and short of that outer side in the retained condition shown". In figures/FIG-2.md change "A small housing, shown schematically, stands proud of the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." to "The mechanical exposure indicator is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." No change to the description or claims is required, and no shape or optional embodiment is to be added to the application text.
- **[major] FIG-3 asserts the space between the cassettes communicates with both guide ducts, but the geometry it describes leaves no path** (figures/FIG-3.md, bullets "Rigid spacer frame 42", "Phase-change cassette 44", "Downward guide duct 48", and the closing) - The brief describes the frame as an upper horizontal web continuous with an outboard upright web at each side, i.e. closed across the full width at the top, with the mating channel 52 formed as a recess in that upper web. It then describes the two cassettes as held within the frame facing one another across the blank space directly above the central inlet opening 46, and each duct 48 as lying outboard of a cassette, between the cassette's outboard surface and the nearer outboard web. On those described elements the inter-cassette space is bounded above by the upper web and at each side by a cassette, so it has no opening into either duct. The brief nevertheless asserts open communication and the disclosed flow sequence through it. This is a verified internal inconsistency in the brief itself, and it would drive a drawing in which the disclosed path "divides along faces of the cassettes, descends through the guide ducts" is broken.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-3.md amend the "Downward guide duct 48" bullet to read: "Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42, each open at its upper end to the blank open space above and between the cassettes 44 and open at its lower end at the bottom of the view." and amend the closing statement to read: "The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and is open at its upper part to the upper end of each duct 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48." This states only the open communication that the disclosed flow sequence itself requires and adds no cassette proportion, no contact, and no new function.

In that attitude the gasket band faces up and forward, not down toward the upper edge 16, and the rib projects toward the viewer rather than downward, so it cannot lie directly above the recess in the module's upper surface. The same bullet set also states that the lid lies above the module on the same upright axis with the parts poised to descend into the shell, which an inverted body cannot do. Three statements in one brief therefore contradict the chosen depiction, leaving the renderer no consistent geometry to draw.
  - Suggested fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, rewrite the affected wording so the inverted attitude is stated once and every relationship is expressed as a closed-condition relationship: change the lid bullet to "Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab, shown schematically, floating above the module 40, matching the shell 10 in plan, shown inverted in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside, shown schematically as a continuous band running around it in register with the upper edge 16, which it meets when the lid 60 is closed."; change the rib bullet to "Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view, shown schematically, the rib 62 entering the recess in the upper surface of the module 40 when the lid 60 is closed."; in the module bullet replace "directly below the depending indexing rib 62" with "positioned to receive the depending indexing rib 62 when the lid 60 is closed"; and change the alignment statement to "The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the inverted lid 60 is drawn above the module 40 on the same upright axis."
- **[minor] Detailed Description asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism inside the guide ducts** (draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Condensate handling and the removable wick", second sentence) - The disclosure states only that openings at the lower ends of the guide ducts discharge condensate into the channel, which supports condensate being present in the ducts and reaching their lower ends. It does not state where the condensate forms, and it does not state that the guide ducts have cooled surfaces. The candidate adds both, asserting an operating mechanism (condensation on cooled duct surfaces) that no affirmative USER passage supplies. The assertion also depends on the figure brief's choice that a cassette surface bounds the duct, which is itself only a drawing convention and is not verbalized in the description.
  - Suggested fix: Replace the sentence with: "Condensate that collects within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56 into the shallow condensate channel 70, rather than standing in the bottom of the interior."
- **[minor] Claim 16 says tray removal exposes the pull tab, where the disclosure and description say the tab remains accessible** (draft/09-claims.md, claim 16, third step; compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Condensate handling and the removab) - The disclosure and the description both express the relationship as the pull tab remaining accessible once the product tray is removed. Claim 16 recasts it as removal of the tray exposing the tab, which implies the tab was previously concealed and is a different relationship from the one the inventor stated. Claims and description must use the same relationship and the same terms for the same feature.
  - Suggested fix: In claim 16 replace "thereby exposing a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray" with "a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel" so the step reads "lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel receiving condensate from condensate discharge openings at lower ends of the downward guide ducts;".

Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.

content.text: I've read every input, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, all six figure briefs, the prior-art index, and the previous QA report, and I checked the workspace for rendered sheets and audit evidence.

input.summary:
Scope note first: the workspace contains **no rendered drawing sheets and no audit evidence**. `figures/` holds only the six Markdown briefs (`FIG-1.md` … `FIG-6.md`); a glob for `**/*.{png,jpg,json}` across the whole workspace returns nothing, so there is no `figures/rendered-*.png` and no `review/figure-audit-evidence.json`. Every pixel-level obligation in the review protocol — visible geometry, printed numerals, leader-to-dot tracing, the FIG. 1 cutting-plane line with its 2-2 designations and rearward arrows, and hatch angles — was therefore impossible to verify, and I report nothing about them. This also explains the already-run mechanical failure listing all 30 numerals as "absent from every drawing": the sheets on which they would print do not exist. I did not re-report that check, the FIG-1 brief length, or the missing-sheet check.

Prior art: `prior_art/INDEX.md` lists `(none)`, and a recursive search of `draft/` and `figures/` finds zero `[REF:...]` citations. The draft cites nothing, so there is no citation to mischaracterise and no citation finding.

Source fidelity is otherwise strong. I traced every claim limitation across all 17 claims (independent claims 1, 12, 16), all 30 entries in `draft/numerals.md`, and every structure, relationship, ordering, and result in the Summary and Detailed Description to an affirmative passage in `input/disclosure.md`. The four bodies, tray feet and lower return passage, inward-spaced tray side walls forming two side supply passages, perforations, the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed cassettes between tray and lid, the central inlet opening / two downward guide ducts / peripheral outlet openings, the full flow sequence and the "no fan, pump, or powered air mover" negative limitation, the rib-into-channel registration and the gasket-seals-after-registration ordering, the resilient feet on the shell ledges, the wick / shallow condensate channel / lower-end discharge openings / pull-tab-accessible relationship, and the entire indicator chain (stem thermally coupled to one cassette, temperature-responsive latch, spring, latched exposed position, irreversibility, manual reset after opening, no airflow control) all trace verbatim or near-verbatim. Both optional features are correctly recited as optional. Naming is consistent throughout, tray feet 22 and resilient feet 54 are kept distinct, each numeral denotes exactly one part in the description, the ledger and every brief, and each brief's "Numerals shown" list exactly matches the numerals in its own body. The abstract is 141 words. All five findings from `review/previous-qa.md` have been applied to the text as suggested — with one leftover, reported below.

Three defects remain: one critical (FIG-2's brief still directs an undisclosed "housing" to be drawn, contradicting its own revised bullet), and two minor (a claim 16 step with no counterpart in the description, and two figure briefs that name numbered parts without applying their numerals). Per the drafting brief, the art supplied to this draft may be incomplete — indeed none was supplied at all.

findings.title: FIG-2 brief still directs an undisclosed indicator "housing" to be drawn, contradicting the same brief's own revised bullet
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md, final paragraph ("Four broken circles..."); compare figures/FIG-2.md bullet "Shell side wall 14"
findings.detail: The previous QA pass removed the undisclosed indicator housing from FIG-2's "Shell side wall 14" bullet, which now reads only: "The mechanical exposure indicator is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." The broken-circle paragraph at the end of the same file was not updated and still instructs the renderer that the fourth enlarged region is "the left shell side wall 14 with its housing and bore at the level of the module 40." Two problems follow. First, no affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or input/conversation.md discloses any housing; the disclosure supplies only "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch." Nothing in the claims, the Summary, the Detailed Description, draft/numerals.md, or FIG-6's revised brief mentions a housing either, so this structure originates solely in a drawing brief. Second, it is an internal contradiction: the possessive "its housing" points back to an element that this file no longer describes anywhere, leaving the renderer with a named solid it has no specification for. FIG-6's corresponding text was corrected to the neutral "the assembly shown schematically within an unnumbered plain outline," so this is the only surviving instance. Because no sheet has been rendered, this brief would still drive the geometry on the next render.

An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch."

No change to the Detailed Description, the Brief Description of the Drawings, or the claims is needed, and no shape, enclosure, or new relationship is introduced.

findings.title: Claim 16 recites withdrawing the indexing rib from the mating channel, a step the Detailed Description never states
findings.where: draft/09-claims.md, claim 16, first step; compare draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Method of passively conditioning a payload", second paragraph
findings.detail: Claim 16's opening step affirmatively recites the rib coming out of the channel as the lid is opened. The Detailed Description describes only that the lid is opened and the module is then lifted out; it never states the converse of the disclosed closing engagement. Every other step of claim 16 has an express counterpart (module lifted out, tray lifted out, pull tab accessible, channel receives condensate from the lower-end discharge openings, wick withdrawn by the pull tab and replaced without opening a cassette, parts returned and lid closed to re-register). Only the rib-withdrawal step is unmatched. The relationship is the direct converse of a disclosed one — input/disclosure.md states "As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame" — so the gap is a drafting omission in the description rather than added matter in the claim, and I mark it minor for that reason.
findings.evidence: draft/09-claims.md, claim 16: "opening an insulated lid of the carrier and withdrawing a depending indexing rib carried by the insulated lid from a mating channel of a rigid spacer frame of a removable thermal module, the rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes and having two downward guide ducts beside the phase-change cassettes;" — versus draft/08-detailed-description.md: "At the destination the insulated lid 60 is opened, the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out, and the removable product tray 20 is lifted out."
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, section "Method of passively conditioning a payload", replace "At the destination the insulated lid 60 is opened, the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out, and the removable product tray 20 is lifted out." with "At the destination the insulated lid 60 is opened, which withdraws the depending indexing rib 62 from the mating channel 52, and the removable thermal module 40 is lifted out and the removable product tray 20 is lifted out." This states only the converse of the already-described closing engagement and adds no new structure.

findings.title: Two figure briefs name a numbered part by its full name but assign no reference numeral to it
findings.where: figures/FIG-5.md, bullets "Shallow condensate channel 70" and "Pull tab 74" and the closing statement; figures/FIG-2.md, bullet "Shell side wall 14"
findings.detail: FIG-5's brief refers three times to "the removable product tray" — the part carried as numeral 20 in draft/numerals.md and used as "removable product tray 20" throughout the Detailed Description, the Summary, and FIG-1 and FIG-2 — but never applies numeral 20, and 20 is absent from FIG-5's "Numerals shown on this figure" list. The tray is unambiguously depicted in that view: its side wall is called out as "Tray side wall 24" and its support as "Tray foot 22", and the closing statement is expressly about the tray's removal. FIG-2's brief likewise names "The mechanical exposure indicator" (numeral 80) without applying the numeral. No numeral is mis-assigned and no part is double-labelled, so this is a coverage and consistency point rather than a mislabel; I mark it minor. It is nonetheless worth correcting before the sheets are rendered, since numerals 20 and 80 must appear on some sheet and these are the natural anchors.
findings.evidence: figures/FIG-5.md: "Shallow condensate channel 70: a shallow upwardly open trough alongside the removable product tray at the bottom of the view, shown schematically." and "The wick 72 lies in the trough of the channel 70 along its length, and the tab 74 is drawn so as to be accessible from above when the removable product tray is removed." — figures/FIG-2.md: "The mechanical exposure indicator is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall." — draft/numerals.md: "| 20 | removable product tray |" and "| 80 | mechanical exposure indicator |"
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-5.md, write "the removable product tray 20" at each of the three occurrences and add "- 20" to that file's "Numerals shown on this figure" list. In figures/FIG-2.md, write "The mechanical exposure indicator 80 is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14..." and add "- 80" to that file's list (the broken-circle paragraph is corrected to match under the FIG-2 housing finding above). No geometry, shape, or relationship changes.
